If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast peak by 2–5% in mid-horizon (days 15–25) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast trough by 2–5% in early-horizon (days 1–10) to avoid underestimating downside risk.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, dampen forecast volatility by 10–15% across all horizons to smooth out overfitting.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows strong upward bias, subtract 1–3% from forecast at day 20+ to correct for momentum overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast shows strong downward bias, add 1–3% to forecast at day 10+ to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast is erratic, apply a 5–10% smoothing filter across all horizons to reduce noise amplification.
